title: Turn a loose Asimov humanoid leg onto its back, seat its knee side plate flush, then start and tighten two M3 bolts
keywords: side plate on M3 heat-set inserts
start and drive M3 bolts with a hex bit
instruction: Turn the leg onto its back, seat the knee side plate flush in its pocket, then start and tighten M3 bolts in the two holes on its long axis nearest its narrow end, and move both hands clear.
context: Robotics technicians assemble humanoids from makers' guides; Menlo's open-source Asimov 1 is built this way, in a market of about 7,000 humanoids sold in 2025 (IFR) or 13,000 shipped (Omdia). Left Leg Step 8: turn the leg so the thigh's bearing faces up, fit side plate 600_08A on housing 600_10C so the protrusion fits the bearing and all holes align with the threaded inserts, then lightly tighten M3x10 flat bolts into the inserts. The 3.03 kg leg (twice the arm's 1.5 kg payload) lies loose on its side and is tipped onto its back, not lifted. Three fits meet on one axis within 5 mm: plate in pocket 0.3 mm a side, pad 34.8 in 35.0 mm bore, boss 11.85 in 12.0 mm bearing; a cocked plate puts its holes off the inserts and no bolt starts. Then a hex driver takes a 3 mm bolt on its magnetic bit, sets it square on its insert's first thread and turns it in, 9 turns of 0.5 mm pitch with the bit pressed in a 2 mm hex socket, until the head is down and snug; then a second bolt.
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of the table. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. All parts are from Menlo's Asimov 1 repository (github.com/menloresearch/asimov-1, CERN-OHL-S-2.0): shapes from the maker's STEP files (the thigh from the maker's URDF mesh). Leg, as after the guide's instruction 3, off the body and loose on the table, nothing holding it: the thigh assembly (URDF left_hip_yaw_link: 1.949 kg, with its centre of mass and inertia) slotted into the knee housing 600_10C (MJF PA12, 1,069.5 cm3 at 1.01 g/cm3: 1.080 kg; the URDF's 2.48 kg knee link includes the calf's later parts), 3.03 kg in all and 54 cm long. Its knee joint is free: the housing turns on the thigh about the bearing's axis, from straight to 1.50 rad bent (URDF), against the unpowered knee actuator's published friction, 0.70 N m to start it and 0.02 N m once it moves, with 0.034 kg m2 reflected inertia (Menlo's actuator table, EC-A4315-P2-36, docs.menlo.ai/asimov/1/reference/joint-design-and-actuation). It starts straight, lying on its side along y with the shank toward -y, the housing's outer face (the plate side) upright and facing away from the robot (+x), the pocket's centre at (46, -7), 6.3 cm up. On its back, the task's turned pose, it rests on three points with that face up, about 4 degrees off level, the pocket's centre at about (31, -6), 10.3 cm up: from its side it tips 86 degrees toward the robot over its lower edge, its centre of mass rising from 6.2 to 7.9 cm (over the edge at 38 degrees) and falling to 5.3. In the outer face, the pocket for the plate: 5.0 mm deep, the plate's own outline with 0.3 mm clearance (80.0 mm across its round end, 40.0 mm across its neck, its narrow end toward the shank), with a 35.0 mm bore at its centre and nine M3 threaded inserts. Its walls stand full depth round the round end and the neck's root and fall away along the neck, where the housing's surface curves down. The thigh's flanged bearing 600_11X (12.0 mm bore, 5.0 mm wide) is on the pocket's axis, its face 11 mm below the housing's face. Plate 600_08A: aluminium 7075, a 5.0 mm sheet 149.4 mm long, 79.4 mm across its round end and 39.4 mm across its neck, 1 mm chamfers on its edges; on one face a 34.8 mm pad (5 mm), a 15 mm step (1 mm) and an 11.85 mm boss (5 mm, 0.9 mm tip chamfer); nine 3.2 mm countersunk holes; 120 g (42.6 cm3 at 2.81 g/cm3). It starts boss down in the socket (36 mm across, 12 mm deep) of an acetal kitting post 50 mm across and 30 mm tall at (20, -17), its sheet on the post's rim, its narrow end toward -y. Friction 0.3 (PA12 and aluminium on the table, on acetal and on each other). Fasteners and tool: nine steel M3x10 flat bolts, DIN 7991 (3.0 mm thread, 0.5 mm pitch, head 6.0 mm across, 1.7 mm tall, 2 mm hex socket), stand head up, tips down, in a printed bolt stand at (13, -25): a 40 x 40 x 8 mm deck with nine 3.2 mm holes on a 12 mm grid, and beside it on the robot's side a tower 34 mm square and 44 mm tall whose 14 mm hole holds a Bahco 808050S stubby ratchet screwdriver (95 mm, magnetic 1/4 in bit holder, 90 g) bit down, fitted with a Wera 840/1 Z Hex-Plus 2.0 x 25 mm bit (05056305001), 13 mm of it out of the holder. The stand with its bolts is one loose 50 g body. Nine brass M3 heat-set inserts, 4.4 mm across and 4.5 mm long, sit in the housing's insert bores (STEP), 0.5 mm under the pocket's floor, under the plate's nine holes. Both arms start at their ready pose. The demo grips at 38 N a finger and presses about 10 N. Real-trial protection and a low-cost stand-in (printed, ballasted to 3.03 kg, pin hinge with a friction screw, gauge-pin fits) are in the README.
scoring: Measured at the end with an inclinometer on the housing's face, a depth gauge (0.01 mm) on the plate's top and each bolt head against the face, a 2.4 mm pin gauge, and a torque screwdriver set to 0.30 N m that clicks before the bolt turns; turns are read by head height (4.5 mm proud at the start, 3.5 mm after 2 turns). Score 0 if the plate or the leg falls off the table. Rungs are cumulative: 0.2 with the leg on its back on the table (the face within 10 degrees of level, at its resting height within 12 mm: lying there, not held up); 0.4 with the plate seated flat (every point of its top within 0.5 mm of flush, tilt under 1 degree, boss down, every hole with no bolt in it within 0.45 mm of its insert's axis; a hole with a bolt in it is read by its bolt); 0.6 with that and one bolt, in one of the two holes on the plate's long axis nearest its narrow end, started on its insert by the robot and driven at least 2 turns by the bit; 0.8 with both; 1.0 with both bolts home (head within 0.5 mm of the face and snug at 0.30 N m), no gripper within 10 cm of the plate or within 8 cm of the leg's centre line, and the plate and leg still, held for 1 s and still true at the end. A plate set in the pocket before the leg was on its back, pressed home with the leg moved 15 mm or its face turned 3 degrees from how it lay when the plate first reached the pocket's mouth, or never carried by a gripper, scores at most 0.2. The bolt rungs read the plate as seated at the same moment.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz; plate, pocket, bearing as maker STEP, no collider widened (fits 0.30/0.10/0.075 mm a side). Friction 0.3. Each bolt: a slider on a 40 kN/m seat spring plus a hinge; it starts only with the plate within 1 mm of flush and the hole within 0.6 mm of its insert, square within 5 deg, turns only with the bit in its socket within 0.9 mm, 10 deg, pushed 5 N; 0.5 mm per turn, 0.10 N m running, 0.30 N m snug after 9 turns. Bit picks a steel bolt by touch (magnet). No cross-threading.
scores: Scripted demo on three RTX 3090 Ti PCs: 0.6, 0.6, 0.4 (one bolt started and driven about 5.9 turns; none on the 0.4 PC); no run reaches 0.8. Dream-1: 0.0 on the revised scene and instruction, no bolt touched. Dream-1 film: 0.0, a run on the earlier version of this task (before the bolts).
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials, unscrew the two bolts and stand them back in the bolt stand, lift the plate out by its neck's flats and set it boss down in the kitting post's socket, straighten the knee and tip the leg back onto its side, plate side away, on its tape marks, and stand the screwdriver bit down in the stand's tower.
